title: PET for Perfusion of the Heart
service: PET myocardial perfusion imaging (Rubidium-82 or ammonia N-13)

criteria.text: Known or suspected coronary artery disease
criteria.span: noninvasive imaging of the perfusion of the heart for the diagnosis and management of patients with known or suspected coronary artery disease

criteria.text: Performed at rest or with pharmacological stress
criteria.span: PET scans performed at rest or with pharmacological stress
using the FDA-approved radiopharmaceutical Rubidium 82 (Rb 82) are covered
using the FDA-approved radiopharmaceutical ammonia N-13 are covered

criteria.text: Performed in place of, not in addition to, SPECT
criteria.span: The PET scan, whether at rest alone, or rest with stress, is performed in place of, but not in addition to, a single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT)

criteria.text: Or following an inconclusive SPECT, where PET is necessary to determine the required medical or surgical intervention
criteria.span: The PET scan, whether at rest alone or rest with stress, is used following a SPECT that was found to be inconclusive. In these cases, the PET scan must have been considered necessary in order to determine what medical or surgical intervention is required to treat the patient.

criteria.text: Inconclusive = equivocal, technically uninterpretable, or discordant with other clinical data; must be documented in the beneficiary's file
criteria.span: an inconclusive test is a test(s) whose results are equivocal, technically uninterpretable, or discordant with a patient's other clinical data and must be documented in the beneficiary's file

notes: Coverage is limited to rest or pharmacological-stress PET; the NCD does not cover exercise-stress PET, and it names only Rb-82 and ammonia N-13 as radiopharmaceuticals. Cases do not use other PET perfusion tracers, whose status this NCD does not address. The pre-July 2001 claim-form requirements are obsolete and not tested.
